project.title: Identification of DCTPP1 interacting proteins by LC-MS/MS
project.projectDescription: To characterize the protein interactome of DCTPP1 in HTR-8 cells, immunoprecipitation (IP) assays were executed. Samples underwent LC-MS/MS analysis coupled with label-free quantification for interactome profiling.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Total cellular lysates were incubated with an anti-HA tag antibody throughout the night. Subsequently, 20 µl of pre-washed Dynabeads™ A were introduced into the mixture, followed by an additional 3-hour incubation at 4 °C. Post-incubation, the beads were pelleted and rinsed thrice using lysis buffer. Bound proteins were eluted by heating the beads at 95 °C for 5 minutes in 2× SDS buffer. Eluted proteins were separated via SDS-PAGE.  The gel was sectioned into approximately 1 mm³ fragments to facilitate in-gel digestion. These gel fragments were sequentially washed with deionized water, 50% acetonitrile (ACN), and 100% ACN. Gel-embedded proteins were reduced, alkylated, and subjected to proteolytic digestion at 37 °C for 12 hours. Digestion was terminated with 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), and the resulting supernatants were transferred to sterile tubes. Residual peptides in the gel were extracted twice with 30% ACN in 1% TFA, followed by a single extraction with 100% ACN. All extracts and supernatants were combined, concentrated by SpeedVac, and purified using a C18 StageTip prior to mass spectrometry analysis.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectrometry data were analyzed using MaxQuant software (Version 1.6.5.0) with default parameters against the UniProt human proteome database. The false discovery rate (FDR) for peptide and protein identification was set at 0.01. Searches were performed with Trypsin/P enzyme specificity, permitting up to two missed cleavages. Carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues was designated as a fixed modification. Variable modifications included methionine oxidation and N-terminal acetylation of proteins.
